body:
## Problem

#494 (PR #524) admits the target checkouts to every interactive spawn through the family's grounding flag (`--add-dir`), derived per session from what its bundles' briefs resolve to. Six of the seven interactive spawn sites carry that grant. One does not.

`run_plan_advisory_batch` re-enters the **planner** for the revision pass when an antagonistic plan review raised findings (`template/src/pdca_harness/leaves.py:3388`):

```python
_invoke(cfg.planner, cfg.root, _plan_revision_prompt(cfg, with_findings), cfg=cfg)
```

No `extra_argv`, so no `_plan_grant(...)` / `_bundle_grant(...)`. Compare the two Plan spawns that were fixed:

- `do_plan`, `leaves.py:922-924` — `extra_argv=_plan_grant([d], cfg, cfg.profile(cfg.planner))`
- `do_plan_batch`, `leaves.py:1115-1117` — `extra_argv=_plan_grant(seeded, cfg, cfg.profile(cfg.planner))`

## Why it matters

The revision session is the one that most needs the checkout. Its inputs are the `plan-advisory-*.md` findings, which the plan-reviewer writes against the target source (path:line citations, `$PDCA_TARGET`), and the brief's own root-cause citation, which the planner role prompt tells it to verify with `git -C <checkout>` plus Read/Grep on the checkout. Deciding whether a finding stands or the brief stands means reading that source. With nothing admitted, the target checkout is outside the workspace again, so this session opens with exactly the per-file approval prompts #494 removed from the other six, and for the same reason the approval cannot stick (a hand grant lands in the untracked `settings.local.json`).

It is an opt-in path (only when `[leaves.plan_advisory]` leaves are configured and produced findings), which is presumably why it was missed.

## Proposal

Same shape as the sibling spawns, one line. Every bundle in `with_findings` carries a brief at this point, so `_bundle_grant` resolves each to its own primary checkout; `_plan_grant` gives the same result and falls back to the known targets only when nothing resolves. Either is defensible; `_bundle_grant` is the tighter one for a session that already knows what it is about, which matches the `_bundle_grant` / `_plan_grant` doctrine written at `leaves.py:734-763`:

```python
_invoke(cfg.planner, cfg.root, _plan_revision_prompt(cfg, with_findings), cfg=cfg,
        extra_argv=_bundle_grant(with_findings, cfg, cfg.profile(cfg.planner)))
```

## Verification

A test alongside the #494 ones: configure a plan-advisory leaf that writes a finding, run `run_plan_advisory_batch` with a fake planner that records its argv, and assert the argv carries `--add-dir <resolved checkout>` for each bundle with findings, and nothing for a bundle whose checkout does not resolve (the scope guard from #494 must hold here too).
title: Plan-advisory revision pass spawns the planner without the #494 workspace grant
